response.justification: Strong, broad engineering background with real high-throughput distributed systems experience (millions of HTTP requests/sec at Sociomantic/dunnhumby), current Staff-level title, and directly relevant hands-on work with AI-agent infrastructure and MCP tooling — which matches the AI-native mindset requirement well. The main gap is the must-have 'strong Python': Python appears nowhere in the skills list or job history, with the depth instead in TypeScript/Node and DLang. Evidence of technical strategy ownership, cross-functional stakeholder management, and on-call/incident response is also thin relative to a Staff IC role with strategy responsibilities. Worth a screening call to probe Python depth and scope of technical leadership.
strengths: Proven high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems work (millions of req/sec)
Hands-on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP/developer tooling experience
Deep craftsmanship: TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based dev, plus open-source tooling and teaching
concerns: No demonstrated Python experience despite it being a must-have
Limited evidence of technical strategy scope, stakeholder management, or on-call ownership
Breadth-heavy profile (web/mobile/embedded) may dilute depth in distributed architecture at scale
